_note: ILLUSTRATIVE RULES for the midterm prototype. They turn a detected IFC change into extra work per RIBA stage. They are documented assumptions (scenario inputs), not a trained model. Replace with practice / contractor data.

design_rework_days_per_channel._why: Re-detailing and re-issuing Stage 4 information. A rename (attribute only) needs no rework; a geometry change needs re-coordination of the opening, structure and facade. Counted once per IFC type: similar elements (e.g. 7 footings) are revised in one design package.

procurement_extra_days._why: A changed specification means a new quotation / certified product; a changed size means a bespoke unit with a longer manufacturing lead time.

design_feeds._why: The revised design information must be issued before the affected work can start.

risk_levels.HIGH: the stage finishes later AND it is on the critical path after the change
risk_levels.MEDIUM: the stage receives extra work or loses at least half of its float, but its finish does not drive the project
risk_levels.LOW: the stage receives extra work that is fully absorbed by float
risk_levels.NONE: no change touches the stage and its dates do not move
risk_levels.HANDOVER: AT RISK when the V2 handover is later than the contract date (V1 handover + contract_handover_buffer_days); TIGHT when it uses more than half of the buffer

stage4.label: V2 issued at end of Stage 4
stage4._why: normal case: the change is known before procurement and construction start

late.label: V2 issued late, after wall construction
late._why: late change during Stage 5: built work must be opened up and rebuilt (x2 for demolition + rebuild), elements already ordered must be re-ordered (full lead time again)
